newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firmer after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firmer after quiet trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were mixed to firmer in quiet trade on Wednesday with brokers saying most investors had taken to the sidelines amid concerns that a new fuel price hike might drive up annual inflation.
"There's not much buying and even the selling is not that much. Everyone is just sitting... They are really concerned about the fuel price going up," one broker said.

The government on Tuesday announced a rise of six to eight percent in petrol and other fuel prices, citing higher procurement costs which it attributed to last month's confrontations in the Gulf region between Iraq and the U.S.
"We might see some negative effects, such as an increase in inflation rates which might rise," another broker said.
Zimbabwe's annual inflation fell to a three-year low of 17.7 percent in August from 22 percent, fuelling hopes of lower interest rates.

On the stock market on Wednesday, the 57-share index put on 7.59 points to close at 6,901.79, pushed up largely by sugar refinery ZSR's 25-cent gain to 1,275, packaging firm Hunyani's 20-cent rise to 370 and textiler David Whitehead's five cent addition to 60.

Among the losers, tobacco company TSL dropped 20 cents to 550, Colcom shed 10 cents to 290 while battery manufacturer Chloride at 65, discount house at 145, finance group UDC at 215 all eased five cents.

In minings, gold producer Ashanti, nickel company Bindura and Wankie Colliery all traded at previous levels while Falgold lost 10 cents to 150. The seven-counter mining index edged a marginal 0.76 points lower to 1,373.18.
